build: TOSEC disc, Granny's Garden (1983)(4Mation)[GRAN1].ssd (SHA-256 71511f3f...0d60f0), a DFS disc of two BBC BASIC II programs, GRAN1 and GRAN2, both saved from &0E00; analysed at PAGE &0E00, where each part's own relocation (lines 3280 and 2590) puts it

comments.text: Line 100. Its bytes are a statement as BASIC tokenises one, PAGE and GOTO as tokens and 2590 as a line number (&8D), which the tokeniser never does after a REM typed in; but the first byte, at &0E04, is REM (&F4), written by line 110's poke. Before the poke the line sent a program loaded anywhere but &0E00 to the relocation at line 2590 (most likely `IF PAGE<>&E00 GOTO2590`; the token the poke replaced is lost). Now it does nothing.

Line 110, `CLEAR:?&E04=244`: forgets the variables and writes the REM token over line 100's first byte, so that later RUNs (ON ERROR's at line 140 and PROCkey's at line 870) do not test PAGE again; the RUN which ends the relocation has made its test already, at line 100, before it reaches this line. In this copy the byte is 244 already.
Lines 120-130: two REMs, `GRANNY'S GARDEN (C) 4MAT 1983` and `MIKE MATSON`, each after a quotation mark and a teletext colour code (&82 green, &85 magenta), as in Part 1.

Line 140, `ON ERROR RUN:*K.10OLD|MRUN|M`. Everything after ON ERROR on its line is the error handler, so the `*KEY10` that would make BREAK type OLD and RUN is never executed: on an error the handler RUNs first. Played on 14 October 2026: the soft-key buffer at &0B00 is empty in play. As in Part 1, the error handler is how the game gets out of Too many GOSUBs, after 26 journeys on the map, or 25 once the lake has told its name (GOSUB2340 never returns either).
Line 150, as Part 1's: the cursor off (VDU 23,0,10,32), the default windows, a clear screen, paged mode off, and `*FX11,0`, auto-repeat off.

Line 160, the arrays. For the four baby dragons, red, green, blue and yellow (0-3): e() their collars, C() what the food just thrown does to each, c() which are out of their cave, w$(5,4) the words line 1220 prints after a throw, from line 1280: each dragon's liking for each food (loves, hates, sometimes eats) and the food's name, dr$() and q$() their names; name$() and ps$(), the children and their passwords.

Line 170, from the DATA at line 740: name$, ps$ and dr$ for 0-3 (Esther, snow, red; Tom, sky, green; Clare and Anna, river, blue; Jessica and Daniel, no password, yellow), and q$(w), `The` and the dragon's colour code and name and `dragon`, with each collar off.

Lines 180-190: Part 2's flags and shared sentences. For the Land of Mystery: jess% and dan% (found), fed% (never set TRUE anywhere), water%, name% (the lake's name heard), key%, keytake%, cake%, caketake%, fire% (TRUE, burning), stone (0, 1 carried, 2 given to the dwarf), giant%, beast%; np=10, where the player is to begin with, which is no place. f$, w$ and v$ are runs of solid graphics for the pictures; q3$, d1$-d3$, l$, w1$ and c1$ are sentences or parts of them; h$ (`The`) and k$ (`dragon`) are set and never read.
Line 200: place$(1-5) from line 770, forest, cottage, lake, castle and hill: the names line 1650 prints after `You are at the`.
Lines 210-220, `Ready to start?`, asked until the answer begins with Y. As in Part 1, an answer ending in f turns the music off (on% FALSE); Part 2 has no T for the trees.
Line 230, the title: `Granny's Garden` and `Part 2` between two rows of asterisks, and the theme tune (PROCsnd1) if on%.
Line 240: `Welcome to the KINGDOM OF THE MOUNTAINS`, double height on a background (colour 29, New Background, gives the code 157).

Lines 250-290, the password, which Part 2 cannot do without: up to seven letters, matched by INSTR against `ky` and `iv` (line 750), so sky (Z=2) and river (Z=3) are taken, and so is any answer with ky or iv after its first letter (`Olive` gives Z=3); snow, or any other answer, gets `Please try again.` (line 300) and the question again. The children found so far are listed and the next named; Z=2 leads to the City of the Dragons (PROCdragon), Z=3 to the Land of Mystery (PROCmap).
Line 300, a GOSUB from the password: `Please try again.` and the space bar.
PROCc: VDU 26 and 12, the default windows and a clear screen.

PROCp(c), Part 2's pause: c half-seconds, timed by the clock (TIME=0, then wait until TIME equals c*50), where Part 1's PROCp counts a FOR loop. BASIC uses this definition, the first from PAGE; the second, at line 630, never (its PROC table in play points here).
PROCh(col,zz,yy,Z$), double-height text, as Part 1's: CHR$141, the colour code CHR$(col+128) and Z$ at column zz on rows yy and yy+1.

PROCsp (lines 340-350), wait for the space bar: *FX15,0 empties every buffer, the keyboard's and the sound queues alike, so a note still playing stops; then `(space bar)` at column 12 and a loop until GET returns 32.
PROCs(col,y): a colour code at column 2 of row y, then PROCsp.
PROClcase(i$) (lines 370-400): inp$ is i$ with the capitals A-Z made lower case.
PROCb(t,b,k1,k2) (lines 410-440), as Part 1's: from where the cursor is, the control code k1, and k2 after it if k2>0, at that column on b-t+2 rows one under the other; t and b set only the count.
PROCup: a text window over rows 0-8, the cursor at its bottom, then eight line feeds with a pause between, so only the top nine rows scroll up; then the default windows.

PROCi(col,x,y,len) (lines 460-530), the game's own input, as Part 1's: only letters, DELETE and RETURN count, the first letter is a capital and the rest lower case, and once the cursor reaches column len the next key, RETURN included, is taken as DELETE, so the field holds len-x-1 letters. A DELETE in an empty field still counts, as in Part 1, and in$ then differs from the screen: l falls below 0 and LEFT$(in$,l) keeps the whole string.

PROCrav1 (lines 540-550), the raven arriving, as Part 1's: the bird's pieces from the DATA at line 760, printed four times down the screen behind conceal codes (152) and shown by PROCt a band at a time, two rows and then the row below, each hidden again before the next, so one small bird flaps its way down the screen.
PROCrav2 (lines 560-590), the raven, cyan, at the bottom of the screen; a pause, then sixteen line feeds scroll it to the top.
PROCt (lines 600-610), Part 1's PROCn: shows a row pair (G=1) or the row below it (G=2) by writing cyan graphics (150) at its start, waits, then hides it with conceal (152).
Line 620, a GOSUB from PROCrav1: H$ from DATA values d to e, each plus 160.
Line 630, a second DEFPROCp with no parameters. It is never used: BASIC takes the first DEFPROCp it finds from PAGE, at line 320, and line 620 ends with RETURN, so nothing runs into it.
PROCwitch (lines 640-720), the Witch, as in Part 1; lines 640-680 draw her, in profile with one eye, and with on% FALSE the eye is shown once, with no sound.

Lines 690-700, the Witch with sound: three times, five notes on channel 1, all at pitch 1, with ENVELOPE 1 redefined before each (Q=10 to 90 a step), and a note on channel 2, while her eye changes, then her mouth opening and closing. In the first round the five notes are queued at once; in the second and third the queue still holds the earlier notes, and the last two or three SOUNDs each wait about a second for room, which holds up her eye and mouth too. Each note plays the envelope as it stands while the note plays, not as it was when queued: the first note's steps grow as BASIC redefines it, and later notes play the latest definition (recorded). The pauses are Part 2's PROCp, by the clock.

Lines 710-720: `Ha ha! Now I've got you! I will send you home at once.`, the raven, `I am very sorry but the Witch has sent us home. You will have to try again later.`, and PROCkey: S starts Part 2 again.
Line 730, DATA 2,8,31,10,35,20,10,9: Part 1's places for the kingdom's trees (Part 1 line 2380). Every READ in Part 2 follows a RESTORE to another line, so nothing reads it: a leftover.

Line 740, DATA: each child or pair of children, their password (blank for Jessica and Daniel), and the colour of the baby dragon with the same number, the colour code first (&81 red, &82 green, &86 cyan for blue, &83 yellow). The blue dragon is drawn cyan too (line 1310).
Line 750, DATA: `ky` and `iv`, the fragments of sky and river (line 260).
Line 760, DATA: the 45 values of the bird PROCrav1 draws, Part 1's line 2420.
Line 770, DATA: the five places' names (line 200).
PROCclare(a,b), Clare's picture, at column a, row b.
PROCjess(a,b), Jessica's picture.
PROCdan(a,b), Daniel's picture.
PROCanna(a,b), Anna's picture.
PROCes(a,b), Esther's picture, Part 1's.
PROCtom(a,b), Tom's picture, Part 1's.

PROCfind(col,c2,c3) (lines 840-850): `Well done! You have found`, name$(Z), steady, since PROCh prints it from column 10 over the flash codes put at column 13, and `Remember this password:` with ps$(Z). Only Clare and Anna are found by it, with the password river.
PROCkey (lines 860-870): `(Key S to start again)`, GET until S or s, and RUN; its UNTIL closes the caller's REPEAT.

PROCsnd1 (lines 880-900), the theme tune, Part 1's: 103 steps from line 910, a pitch n and a length t (t=1 when n is 0), each length divided by 1.5, played at A+96 on channel 1, given as &00011 so that each note starts at once and the channel runs ahead of the other two, and at A and A+48 on channels 2 and 3, silent when n is 0, where A=(n+5)*4.
Lines 910-920, DATA: the theme tune, the same values as Part 1's lines 3230-3240.

PROCdragon (lines 930-1260), the City of the Dragons, from the password sky. Lines 930-970: the raven, `Are you brave enough to look for them?` (anything but Y: `I'm sure you are really.`), the land (PROCland), a wait of up to four seconds (INKEY400), the space bar, and the Keeper of the Gates.
Lines 980-1010: Ah-Choo, the Keeper of the Gates: `What is your favourite food?` (up to 37 letters), `Whenever I have` the answer `I start to sneeze.`, three sneezes; then Anna, lost, who comes too.

Lines 1020-1040, the two big dragons: drawn twice, then `These big dragons are going off to hunt for their dinner.`; then the screen moves sideways a column at a time, 39 times, by VDU 23,0,13,q, which writes the CRTC's register 13, the low byte of the screen's start, as each column's colour codes are rewritten.

Lines 1050-1100: the four baby dragons guarding Clare (PROCdrag), four magic collars, one dragon at a time, and the food: 3 bags of chips, 3 oranges, 3 lollies and 3 buns. `If you run out of something the Witch will come.`

Lines 1110-1230, the dragons tamed. Each throw is one letter (PROCi(6,18,9,20)) matched against the records at line 1270; an unknown letter gets `Please try again.` B, C, O and L count the buns, chips, oranges and lollies thrown, and a fourth of any one brings the Witch. Each food adds 1 to one dragon and takes 1 from another (buns: red out, yellow in; lollies: green out, red in; oranges: blue out, green in; chips: yellow out, blue in), each kept between 0 (in) and 1 (out). The dragons out are drawn, four sentences say who loves, eats or hates the food, and when exactly one is out it gets a collar. The loop ends when all four have one.
Lines 1240-1260: all four collared, Clare rescued from the cave, and PROCfind with Clare and Anna and the password river; then PROCkey.
Line 1270, DATA: five records of a food's letter and what it does to the four dragons, +1 out and -1 in: B, L, O, C, and B again, which only makes a fifth read for an unknown letter.

Lines 1280-1290, DATA: w$(1-5,1-4), five groups of four, one item for each food in the order B, L, O, C: the red dragon's verbs (loves, hates, sometimes eats), the foods' names after the colour code &85, then the green, blue and yellow dragons' verbs.

PROCdrag(a) (lines 1300-1370): baby dragon a at column a*10 in its colour, 145 red, 146 green, 150 cyan (the blue dragon) or 147 yellow, with its collar if e(a)=1, in a window over rows 0-10. The first statement, col=col+144, is overwritten before col is used; line 1340 changes nothing for a of 0-3.
PROC1(tp): a text window from row 0 to row tp.
PROC2(bt): a text window from row bt to row 24.
Line 1400, a collar printed at dragon m's column: after PROC2's ENDPROC, and no GOTO or GOSUB names it, so it never runs.
PROCland (lines 1410-1470): the land of the dragons, in teletext graphics, with a band of solid blocks along the bottom.
PROCcl: one magic collar, three rows of graphics sent with VDU and cursor moves.
PROCkeeper(s): a magenta strip on row 12 for the Keeper of the Gates to stand on and a window over rows 0-11, then s times his face (PROCkp) and a sneeze (PROCk).
PROCkp(x,y): the keeper's face, eight rows at column x, row y.
PROCk(x,y), one sneeze: ten flickers of the keeper's feet, the two green cells PROCkp draws under his face (row y+7), then his face redrawn at the top of the window with his head thrown back.
PROCmap (lines 1520-1540), the Land of Mystery, from the password river: the raven, `Come with me to the Land of Mystery.`, the map with a red cross, and the first choice (PROCw).

Lines 1550-1590, one place each, the targets of PROCw's ON np GOSUB: the forest, the cottage, the lake, the castle and the hill. A place that returned would run on into the next line's; every way out of each ends in PROCw, the Witch or the end, so none does.
Line 1600, DATA: `or`, `ot`, `ak`, `as`, `il`, the fragments that recognise forest, cottage, lake, castle and hill (PROCw, line 1670).
PROCmp (lines 1610-1630), the map of the Land of Mystery: the five places, the paths between them, and `LAND OF MYSTERY`.

PROCw (lines 1640-1750), every journey: op=np, the map, `You are at the` place (except on the first journey, from the start, op=10), and `Where do you wish to go?`, matched by INSTR (the last match wins). The places are numbered forest 1, cottage 2, lake 3, castle 4, hill 5, and the sum of where the player is and where they go picks the road: 6 has none (forest and hill, cottage and castle), and from the start (op=10) only the forest and the cottage are open; 4 meets the dwarf, 8 the troll, 9 the beast, and 5 (forest and castle, cottage and lake) is `not a good idea` and brings the Witch. Then ON np GOSUB. The GOSUB never returns, so the 27th journey, or the 26th once the lake has told its name (GOSUB2340 never returns either), stops with Too many GOSUBs and ON ERROR starts Part 2 again.

PROCcastle (lines 1760-1800), the Castle of Dreams: the keeper (PROCeyes), the door (PROCdoor), `Are you ready to explore?` N leaves; anything but Y goes back to line 1750 and into PROCcastle again, where the keeper, who has the cake, asks for another. Y: the dream (PROCdream), and Daniel. With Jessica found as well it is the end (PROCfin).

PROCdoor (lines 1810-1840), the castle door. Without the key, the Witch. With it, the door opens and the key is kept. The second branch, dan% (Daniel found) and `The lock has been changed.`, cannot be reached: a second visit never gets past the keeper (PROCeyes).

PROCcott (lines 1850-1890), the cottage: its picture, `You are outside a cottage.`, and the key on every visit until it is taken (PROCkeytake); after that `Do you want to go inside?` N back to the map, Y inside (PROCincot), anything else asks again.

PROCincot (lines 1900-1930), inside the cottage. The cake once taken (caketake%), the Witch is coming (PROCwitchcome). Otherwise the Witch is there with a cake: Y takes it (cake%, caketake%), N sends the player out, anything else asks again.

PROCkeytake (lines 1940-1970), the key on the ground, offered on every visit to the cottage until it is taken: K takes it (key%, keytake%), G goes inside (PROCincot) and leaves it, anything else asks again. There is one key.
PROCwitchcome: `The Witch is coming! You had better go, quickly.`, and back to the map; the Witch does not come.

PROChill (lines 1990-2060), the high hill: its picture with fifteen white stones at random places, what can be seen, whether the forest is still smoking (fire%), the giant on every visit until he is answered Y (PROCgiant), and a stone: while one is carried (stone=1) nothing more, otherwise `Do you want to take one?`, Y sets stone=1.

PROCgiant (lines 2070-2090), the hungry giant: `Shall I eat you?` N runs away to the map; Y: `I don't really eat people. Well, not many.` and giant% is set. Anything else asks again by calling PROCgiant inside itself; when that returns, line 2090 ends and BASIC passes over line 2100 as a DEF and runs Creepy Forest's body from line 2110, inside PROCgiant: no stone is offered, and the map then says the player is at the hill (played on 14 October 2026, `reference/p2-28-the-giant-runs-into-the-forest.png`).

PROCfor (lines 2100-2160), Creepy Forest: 72 Pompom trees (PROCwd) at random rows, and the litter notice. The fire once out, the Witch. Burning, without water: `Fetch some water from the lake.` With water: the fire is put out (fire% FALSE) and the tower is next (line 2150).

Lines 2150-2160, the tall tower behind the fire: `Do you want to go in?` N goes back to the map, which loses Jessica, since the forest now brings the Witch; anything else but Y asks again; Y finds Jessica, and with Daniel found too it is the end (PROCfin), otherwise `Now you must find Daniel.`
PROCwd: one Pompom tree, two rows of graphics.

PROClake (lines 2180-2270), the lake, Redhorn. With water already taken, `This is my lake.` and back. Otherwise `Have you come for water?` N asks whether to hear its name (PROCname) on every visit until it has been heard; Y wants the key first (PROCeatkey), then gives water (water%) and offers its name. Line 2200's test (water and the key both held) cannot be met, as the water costs the key, and line 2270 is never reached: it needs the name heard first, which costs the key, and line 2260's PROCeatkey then never returns.
PROCeatkey (lines 2280-2300): `I want a key to eat, first.` Without the key, back to the map. With it, `Can I have your key, please?` N back to the map, Y and the key is gone (key% FALSE).

PROCname (lines 2310-2340): `Do you want to know my name?` With water already taken, Y tells it, `Redhorn`. Without, Y asks for the key first (PROCeatkey) and tells it only once the key is handed over: the key is gone and no water given, and there is no other key, so the castle door and the fire are out of reach for good (played on 14 October 2026). PROCnext, named after the first GOSUB, is defined nowhere, and line 2340 ends in PROCw, so it is never called.

PROCtroll (lines 2350-2380), on the road between the lake and the hill, each way and each time: `what sort of trees grow in the forest`, passed by any answer with `pom` in it after its first letter, which PROCi makes a capital (`Pompom` passes, `pom` does not); otherwise np=op and back to the map.

PROCdwarf (lines 2390-2410), on the path between the forest and the lake: nothing while stone=2 (paid, and no stone taken from the hill since); without a stone, `bring me a stone from the hill` and back; with one, thanks, and stone=2.

PROCwi(k1,k2): a clear screen and the frame the troll, the dwarf and the beast are drawn in: k1, and k2 after it, at column 12 of rows 1-10, a black background (156) at column 29, and a window of columns 13-31, rows 1-11, for the picture.

PROCbeast (lines 2430-2460), on the road between the castle and the hill: `Hello again.` once passed; otherwise `My brother lives in water. What is his name?`, passed by any answer with `horn` in it after its first letter, which PROCi makes a capital (Redhorn, the lake; `horn` alone does not pass); otherwise np=op and back.

PROCeyes (lines 2470-2520), the Keeper of the Castle of Dreams: `I am watching you!` and the eyes (PROCI). fed% is never TRUE, so line 2500's greeting never shows. `I am hungry.`: with the cake, it is taken (cake% FALSE) and the keeper lets the player on; without, `bring me a cake.` and back to the map. Line 2520 is never reached. There is one cake, so the castle is entered on its first visit with the cake or never.
PROCI (lines 2530-2540), the keeper's eyes: seven times, rows 2-6 hidden one by one with conceal (152), then shown again from the bottom in a new colour, red to white (143+f).

PROCdream (lines 2550-2560), the dream: the keeper four times with the screen's start moved (VDU 23,0,13), the scroll, Anna's picture over and over with each baby dragon, the land, and Jessica, always magenta, drawn down the screen at seven columns from left to right, each column's rows given a new background colour.

PROCfin (lines 2570-2580), the end: `That's the end of the adventure. I hope you enjoyed it.`, `T H A N K Y O U`, flashing (&88, Flash, before the T and no Steady after it), with a colour code before each of the other letters, and all six children, the theme tune, played whatever on% holds, `And Granny says it's time for tea.`, and PROCkey.

Lines 2590-2600, the relocation that line 100 no longer reaches, as Part 1's: `*TAPE`, the program copied to &0E00, TOP's high byte lowered, PAGE=&E00 and RUN. The analysis runs it with `GOTO2590` after LOAD (orientation.md).
